summary: Frontend-only targeted retest of SettingsDrawer fixes (v33). BUG FIX 1 (remove drawer-support-call / tel: row): PASSES for both customer and barber — the element does not exist, no <a href='tel:...'> is present inside the drawer, and only settings-support-whatsapp remains under 'الدعم'. BUG FIX 2 (white row labels for luxury dark contrast): FAILS for both roles. The computed color of every row label span (.flex-1 inside drawer-pw-toggle, update-location-btn, settings-support-whatsapp, link-about, link-contact, link-help, link-share-app, link-privacy, link-terms) is rgb(26, 26, 26) — dark grey — NOT white. Since the dark rows still render at bg-[#111] (rgb(17,17,17) — bg-[#111] is NOT in the light-theme override list), the labels are effectively invisible (dark grey on near-black), matching the original bug report. The developer's belt-and-suspenders `text-white` on both the button and the span has no effect because /app/frontend/src/index.css line 164 declares `.text-white { color: #1a1a1a !important; }` as part of a global LIGHT THEME OVERRIDE block (lines 144–213). That override wins on CSS specificity due to `!important`, so no amount of adding `text-white` in JSX will fix this. Also note the drawer aside was styled bg-[#0a0a0a] but is overridden to rgb(248,248,248), while the row backgrounds bg-[#111] are NOT overridden (still rgb(17,17,17)) — this mismatch (light drawer + dark rows + dark text) is what creates the invisible-labels effect visible in the screenshot.

ui_bugs.issue: All row label spans render at computed color rgb(26,26,26) instead of white/near-white. `text-white` utility is neutralized by a global !important override in index.css. Dark grey text on rgb(17,17,17) row background is unreadable — reproduces the original bug the fix was meant to address.
aside bg-[#0a0a0a] is overridden to rgb(248,248,248) (light), but rows bg-[#111] stay rgb(17,17,17) (dark). Design intention (dark drawer) is broken — visually it is light drawer with dark row cards.

issues: Labels invisible on all rows in both customer and barber roles due to CSS specificity conflict — confirmed via getComputedStyle across 9 selectors.

action_items: The FIX MUST BE IN /app/frontend/src/index.css, NOT in SettingsDrawer.jsx. The block titled 'LIGHT THEME OVERRIDE' (lines 144–281) globally sets `.text-white { color: #1a1a1a !important }` (line 164) — which cancels the developer's JSX-level text-white fix. Options: (a) Add a scoped exception before/after that block, e.g. `[data-testid='settings-drawer'] .text-white, [data-testid='settings-drawer'] span.flex-1 { color: #ffffff !important; }` and `[data-testid='settings-drawer'] .bg-\[\#0a0a0a\] { background-color: #0a0a0a !important; }` plus keep bg-[#111] dark; OR (b) Replace `text-white` in SettingsDrawer.jsx label spans with an inline `style={{ color: '#ffffff' }}` which beats the class-level !important; OR (c) introduce a new utility class like `text-luxe-white` that is not overridden and use it on the drawer labels.

Decide the intended drawer theme: the code (bg-[#0a0a0a]/bg-[#111]/text-white) is designed dark, but the app-wide light theme override in index.css converts most surfaces to light. Rows bg-[#111] were not added to the override list, causing a half-migrated look. If the app is supposed to be light-themed overall, add bg-[#111] to the override list AND change the label color intention to a dark tone with white row bg. If the drawer should remain dark (as this fix implies), scope-exempt the drawer from the light theme override as above.
critical_code_review_comments: index.css lines 144–213 apply a very broad, high-specificity light-theme override using !important across .text-white, .text-zinc-200/300/400/500/600, bg-[#050505]/#0a0a0a/#121212/#1a1a1a, borders, inputs, glass, splash, leaflet, and toasts. Any JSX-level color fix on any dark surface will not survive this without inline styles or a scoped exception. This is a fragile pattern — recommend consolidating theming via a proper light/dark CSS variable set instead of one-off overrides.

The override list omits bg-[#111] (used by drawer rows) and bg-[#0f0f0f], while including bg-[#0a0a0a] (used by drawer aside). The inconsistency creates surfaces that are half-migrated — a bug factory for future contrast issues.

SettingsDrawer.jsx is correctly fixed at the JSX layer (drawer-support-call fully removed, text-white applied both on the button and inner span). The developer's work is not at fault — the CSS override is. Suggest documenting the light-theme override in a README or via a comment in JSX warning contributors.

rca of the issue: Root cause: /app/frontend/src/index.css lines 144–213 contain a global 'LIGHT THEME OVERRIDE' block. Line 164 forces `.text-white { color: #1a1a1a !important }`. This has higher specificity than any Tailwind utility applied in SettingsDrawer.jsx. Consequently, the developer's fix (adding `text-white` to DrawerRow button and its .flex-1 span) computes to rgb(26,26,26) at runtime, defeating the intended luxury-white contrast. Additionally, bg-[#0a0a0a] on the drawer aside is remapped to #F8F8F8 (light), but bg-[#111] on the rows is not in the override list and remains rgb(17,17,17), so the row cards stay dark, giving dark-text-on-dark-card => invisible labels. Reproduction: login as either seeded user → /app/settings → click settings-drawer-open → getComputedStyle on any row label span.flex-1 → color === 'rgb(26, 26, 26)'. Mitigation options are listed in action_items.
